01 · Cloud and Serverless

Cloud and Serverless

§ Service Models

Cloud Service Models

Moving right transfers more infrastructure operations to the provider

Serverless ComputingServerless transfers server provisioning and operation to a managed service

The service hides server allocation behind an application interface

The Remaining Responsibilities

Provider managesUser still decides
Servers and service maintenanceData meaning and schema
Service execution infrastructureQueries and access permissions
Service-level scaling mechanismsWorkload design and cost controls
Managed infrastructure still requires deliberate data, access and workload choices

MilestoneWhat became easier

Spark and BigQuery

ToolUser expressesTypical responsibility

ServiceRole

02 · Analytical Warehouses

Analytical Warehouses

§ Query and Storage

Why an Analytical Warehouse

Shared analytical tables connect multiple sources to consistent departmental reports

OLTP and OLAPOnline Transaction Processing (OLTP) and Online Analytical Processing (OLAP)

Small transactional updates and large analytical scans place different demands on storage

Row and Column Layouts

The same logical table can group values by row or by column

The Same Values on Disk

Twelve values retain their meaning while their physical order changes

Point Reads and Analytical Scans

Choose a layout around the values that the workload needs to read

Sales Scan in Row Layout

This full-row scan reads sixteen values to compute a sum of four amounts

Sales Scan in Column Layout

The column scan reads four amounts and returns the same total of 1000

BigQuery Storage and Compute

Persistent table storage and query execution are managed as separate layers

Managed Fault Tolerance

Replicated storage protects against infrastructure failures rather than incorrect analytical logic

Distributed Query Execution

Workers read portions of the table and combine partial results

Partial Sums for Four Sales

Two partial sums produce the same total as one scan over all four sales

Grain of an Analytical Table

Product Sales in SQL

SELECT p.name,SUM(s.amount) AS total
FROM fact_sales AS s
JOIN dim_product AS p USING(product_id)
GROUP BY p.product_id,p.name ORDER BY p.product_id;
nametotal
Chocolate700
Ice-cream300
The same four facts produce Chocolate 700 and Ice-cream 300

Answer: October 3 Product Sales

SELECT p.name,SUM(s.amount) AS total
FROM fact_sales AS s
JOIN dim_product AS p USING(product_id)

Date-Partitioned Sales

A date filter can skip unrelated partitions instead of scanning all sales

03 · Lakes and Lakehouses

Lakes and Lakehouses

§ Files and Tables

Why Keep a Data Lake

Keep diverse source files for later analytical uses

Warehouse, Mart and Lake

StoreOrganizing unitTypical purpose
WarehouseIntegrated analytical tablesConsistent organizational analysis
Data martA subject or department subsetFocused reports
LakeFiles and datasets in varied formatsPreserve and reuse diverse inputs
A mart narrows the analytical scope; a lake broadens the retained source material

Schema on ReadFiles can arrive first, but queries still need structure, types and meaning

{"sale_id":3,"product_id":"P1","amount":"400"}
{"sale_id":4,"product_id":"P2","amount":"100"}
The string "400" needs an explicit numeric interpretation before summing

From Lake to Warehouse

Separate raw and analytical stores introduce copying, transformations and refresh dependencies

ETL and ELTExtract, Transform, Load (ETL) or Extract, Load, Transform (ELT)

Transform before loading, or load detail first and transform inside the warehouse

§ Lakehouse Management

Why a Lakehouse

Lakehouse adds table management over lake files for shared analytical use

Lakehouse Data Preparation

A unified architecture still needs staging, transformations and curated analytical tables

Consistent Table Snapshots

A new snapshot changes October 2 while retaining the unchanged October 3 file

Tools Around a Lakehouse

LayerExamplesRole
Object storageS3, Cloud StorageStore the data files
Columnar file formatParquetEncode values in files
Table formatIceberg, Delta LakeManage table metadata and changes
Compute and platformSpark, DatabricksExecute transformations and analytical queries
Storage, file format, table format and compute belong to different layers

04 · Data Orchestration

Data Orchestration

§ Workflow Definition

Why Data Orchestration

A successful query can still run before its required data is ready

A Data Pipeline

A pipeline carries data; orchestration coordinates the work that moves and transforms it

Airflow at Airbnb

YearDevelopment
2014Maxime Beauchemin starts Airflow at Airbnb
2015Airbnb announces the open-source project
2016The project enters Apache incubation
2019Apache Airflow becomes a top-level project
Airflow grew from a company workflow tool into an Apache project

A Sales Workflow DAGA Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG) defines tasks and their dependencies

Sales and products can load independently; the join waits for both inputs

Dependencies in PythonAirflow dependency notation, with task definitions omitted

copy_sales >> build_facts
copy_products >> build_facts
build_facts >> daily_totals
Both copy tasks are upstream of build_facts

Tasks, Operators and Sensors

ConceptMeaningSales workflow example
TaskOne defined unit of workLoad the sales file
OperatorA template used to create a taskSubmit a SQL query
SensorA waiting task patternWait for the input file
A workflow combines concrete tasks built from reusable execution and waiting patterns

Airflow Control and WorkersHistorical architecture: focus on the responsibilities, rather than deployment details

Scheduling, task execution and recorded state are distinct responsibilities

Airflow Graph ViewHistorical Airflow interface

A real workflow branches into independent tasks and joins dependent results

§ Workflow Execution

Caveat: An Upstream Failure

A failed product load prevents the dependent join from using incomplete inputs

Task States in AirflowHistorical Airflow interface

A workflow run can contain successful, failed and blocked tasks

Task Durations and OverlapHistorical Airflow interface

Overlapping task bars reveal concurrency; long dependent paths can delay completion

Data Interval and Run Time

Data being processedExecution timeMeaning
October 2 salesOctober 3 morningScheduled daily processing
October 2 salesOctober 5 afternoonReprocess a corrected past date
October 3 salesOctober 5 afternoonProcess another date in the same recovery
The date being recomputed can differ from the time when the task runs

Caveat: Retrying an Append

Retrying the same append can count the same sales twice

Answer: Repeatable Date Load

BEGIN;
DELETE FROM daily_sales WHERE sale_date='2025-10-03';
INSERT INTO daily_sales
SELECT sale_date,SUM(amount) FROM fact_sales
WHERE sale_date='2025-10-03' GROUP BY sale_date;
COMMIT;
BEGIN;
DELETE FROM daily_sales WHERE sale_date='2025-10-03';
INSERT INTO daily_sales
SELECT sale_date,SUM(amount) FROM fact_sales
WHERE sale_date='2025-10-03' GROUP BY sale_date;
COMMIT;
SELECT * FROM daily_sales ORDER BY sale_date;
sale_datetotal
2025-10-02500
2025-10-03500
Two replacements leave one correct total for each date

Backfill After a Correction

Recomputing October 2 changes its total to 550 while October 3 remains 500

Success and Data Checks

CheckExpected for this reportFailure caught
One row per sale_date2 distinct dates, 2 rowsRepeated date rows

Execution success and valid analytical data are separate conditions

Orchestration connects ingestion, distributed computation and published analytical results
